children: New Delhi, Sept. 24 -- Latest data from TAM AdEx shows digital advertising impressions rose 44% year-on-year in January-July 2026. Artificial intelligence (AI) companies are helping drive that growth: OpenAI ranked among India's top three digital advertisers, ahead of Google and Facebook. The shift points to a digital ad market that is broadening beyond e-commerce into services, software and technology.
Mint explains what this means for India's advertising market.
Digital advertising is no longer driven primarily by online shopping. Services accounted for 47% of digital ad impressions in January-July, making them the biggest contributor, according to TAM AdEx.
Ecom-Other Services was the largest individual category, with a 10% share of digital ad impressions, replacing Ecom-Online Shopping. Five of the top 10 digital categories were from services.

Growth also extended across other categories. Software advertising rose 51%, while advertising in real estate, travel and tourism, and clothing, textiles and fashion grew 90%, 71% and 39%, respectively.
The numbers suggest digital's strength is increasingly coming from the breadth of businesses using the medium, rather than from a single sector.
More than 111,000 advertisers were exclusive to digital during January-July, highlighting the breadth of the medium.

Adobe Software India was the largest digital advertiser, accounting for 4% of ad impressions, followed by Flipkart and OpenAI at 3% each. Amazon Online India and Reliance Retail accounted for 2% each, while Google and Hindustan Unilever had 1% each.
OpenAI's position is notable: it ranked ahead of Google and Facebook in the January-July rankings as it expands its consumer business in India.
The data points to a digital advertising market attracting a broader mix of services, software and technology companies.
The list includes newer AI and technology companies such as GPAI and Morphic.
Attitudist led the list, followed by Poly Market, GPAI, Keevx, Caffeine Inc, Little Bird, Futureproof Lab Inc, the Institute of Cost Accountants of India, Morphic and Vivimedia.
Their presence shows how digital advertising is bringing in businesses with little or no traditional television advertising footprint.
OpenAI has marketed ChatGPT around major cricket properties, including the IPL and Women's Premier League, as it works to build ChatGPT as a mainstream consumer brand.

OpenAI said in February that India had more than 100 million weekly ChatGPT users. It began rolling out ChatGPT ads to Free and Go users in India in August, initially working with more than 50 brands, and subsequently opened self-service access through its Ads Manager in India.
That creates a two-way advertising opportunity: OpenAI is spending to build ChatGPT's reach among Indian consumers while also developing an advertising business of its own.

AI is creating a new layer in India's advertising market. AI companies are emerging as a new pool of digital-first advertisers, while AI-powered search, voice and agentic discovery are creating new advertising formats.

WPP Media expects intelligence-led formats to grow 8% in India in 2026, even as digital accounts for 68.1% of total ad revenue. Redseer expects AI-native advertising to scale faster than earlier digital formats as AI platforms build large user bases and seek to monetise that attention.
For advertisers, the shift could move competition beyond buying digital reach to influencing how consumers discover brands through AI.
